name: Scratchboard
means: White line scratched out of solid black: the inverse of pen and ink, luminous highlights emerging from darkness.
tags: scratchboard, white lines on black, engraved, high contrast, inverted linework
prose: a scratchboard illustration - fine white lines scratched from a solid black ground, luminous highlight emerging from darkness
works_for: video - high-contrast fine line is a boiling risk
note: The inversion is what makes this interesting and also what makes it fragile: if the model reverts to black-on-white it has produced pencil_sketch, which already exists and measured ready. | Authored in the second wave, after the first 64 were rendered and measured. status=untested because nothing here has been rendered yet - the first wave shipped 46 cards marked ready without a single render and 27 of 64 turned out to be routed to the wrong engine.
verdict: Dark ground with some white line, but it never fully inverted. Partial. A STYLE LoRA WAS TRIED AND FAILED TO INVERT IT: all seven qwen settings stayed dark and nearly monochrome without ever becoming white line scratched out of a solid black ground. illustration at 1.0 gives the strongest engraved line in the set - real etched hatching through the coat and hair - but the ground stays mid-tone, and at 1.5 the darkness is lost entirely and the coat returns olive and brown.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject, on both engines. studio/_tools/style_examples.py --all-engines
